title: robust-quant-sentinel-and-layer-gain-profiling-for-llama-mistral-qwen
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: FP8/INT8 calibration on LLama/Mistral/Qwen family shows intermittent token-level hallucination and increased top-k entropy for ~0.6% of samples in production-like prompts. Root cause analysis points to sparse, transient head/channel outliers that shift layer activation distributions during long-context runs. Existing per-layer static scale inference sometimes underestimates tail mass, causing quantized kernels to saturate or clip critical signals.

Goal: Implement a lightweight per-model "quant sentinel" that detects head/channel activation surges during calibration and produces a conservative layer-gain profile plus a compact set of head exceptions. Integrate the sentinel with the calibration harness so that the final quant profile includes per-layer fallback thresholds and a small set of head-level adjustments. Validate against held-out generation suites (long-context pass, instruction-following, and retrieval-augmented prompts) to ensure <= 0.5% degradation in top-1 token accuracy and <2% increase in avg latency at target batch sizes.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness produces per-layer scaling and head exception list for each model (LLama/Mistral/Qwen)
Held-out generation suite shows delta <= 0.5% top-1 token accuracy compared to FP16 baseline
Quant profile size increase <= 6% (metadata for head exceptions and thresholds)
Automated sentinel runs flag samples where online activation percentile > 99.95 for any head/channel
Runtime honors head exceptions by routing affected requests to conservative quant kernel or FP16 hot-path
PRs merged with tests and end-to-end benchmark results included
steps: Instrument calib-harness to emit per-layer and per-head activation histograms and rolling percentiles (p50,p90,p99,p99.9,p99.95)
Run 2k sample calibration sweep per model using production-ish prompts (mix of short instructions, long-context, RAG examples)
Compute layer gain = max(1, p99.95 / p95) with smoothing window across adjacent layers to avoid oscillation
Identify candidate hot heads where p99.95 > 8 * p95 or absolute activation > model-specific threshold
Serialize profile: {layer_gain[], head_exceptions[(layer,head,threshold)]} and add metadata version tag
Integrate lightweight runtime check: if request triggers head_exceptions during warmup, use conservative kernel (higher scale) or fallback to FP16 hot-path
Run regression suite (perplexity, token-accuracy, rouge) and latency bench at batch sizes 1,8,32 on target GPU types
Collect metrics, iterate thresholds to meet acceptance criteria, and prepare PR + design doc
notes: Trade-offs: enabling head-level exceptions increases profile size and runtime branching. We aim to limit exceptions to <0.5% of heads on average; otherwise consider head grouping heuristics.
Alternate approach considered: dynamic per-request re-scaling using running KL divergence; rejected for now due to runtime jitter and complexity on dedicated pools.
Edge case: models with heavy MoE-like activations (rare in Mistral family) may require different heuristics — add as separate follow-up if observed.
We must ensure sentinel outputs are stable across calibration seeds; use 3 seeds and keep intersection of exceptions as conservative baseline.
If runtime fallback causes latency SLO violations, we will implement a probabilistic fallback that only routes top-K% latency-tolerant requests to FP16 hot-path.
Coordinate with console team for rollout visibility: add 'quant-sentinel' tag in Console per-model profile view
updates: 2026-03-01: Initial prototype added per-head hist emission to calib-harness. Observed 0.9% of samples with head p99.95 spikes on LLama-3-70B during long-context tests.
2026-03-04: Ran three calibration seeds for LLama-3-70B and Mistral-40B. Intersection heuristic reduced head exceptions by ~60% while preserving coverage for recurrent spikes.
2026-03-08: Early runtime integration: conservative kernel increases per-layer scale by 12% on flagged requests; latency increase measured +1.1% at batch=8 on A100-80GB.
2026-03-10: Validation run against generation suite for Qwen-34B shows token-top1 delta = 0.42% vs FP16 baseline, perplexity delta = +0.03. Profile size increased 4.3%.
2026-03-12: Open PR created for runtime changes and unit tests; leaving remaining tasks for end-to-end CI and design doc review by infra and runtime teams.
